Assume countable choice. Let $Y=U_\alpha\cup_\Sigma U_\beta$ be a smooth closed connected oriented three-manifold with $H_2(Y;\mathbb Q)=0$, with a pointed Heegaard diagram whose two complete disk systems each cut its handlebody into one ball. Let $P$ be any integral region domain whose chain boundary is an integral linear combination of the full attaching circles. Then $P=c[\Sigma]$ for an integer $c$. Thus $n_z(P)=0$ implies $P=0$.

In particular the assertion applies to every complete singly pointed Heegaard diagram of a rational homology sphere. Such diagrams satisfy the stronger global mixed-sign admissibility condition: there is no nonzero periodic domain with zero basepoint coefficient. No disk-index formula, existence of regular perturbations, or Floer invariance is asserted. The conclusion concerns singly pointed complete cut systems; it does not assert the same constant-domain formula for multipointed disk systems cutting a handlebody into several balls.

Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma$ be a closed Riemann surface with two systems $\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta$ of $m\ge1$ pairwise disjoint curves in each system, with transverse finite opposite-system intersections. Let $L_\alpha,L_\beta$ be their product tori in $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$. Choose one interior point $a_R$ in each complementary region and exact product charts about every intersection generator, disjoint from the diagonal and every divisor $E_{a_R}$. Consider smooth finite-energy holomorphic strips with uniform generator ends, for paths $J_t$ equal to the standard symmetric-product structure near the diagonal and every $E_{a_R}$. The perturbation paths may have different interior values; the surface, attaching systems, region points and product generator charts are fixed.

For such a strip set $D(u)=\sum_R n_{a_R}(u)[R]$, with the actual integer divisor multiplicities. If $u$ and $v$ have the same ordered generator ends, then
$$\partial(D(u)-D(v))=\sum_i A_i\alpha_i+\sum_j B_j\beta_j$$
for integers $A_i,B_j$, as a full oriented curve-chain identity. Thus $D(u)-D(v)$ is a periodic domain in the full-curve sense, not merely a homologically periodic chain. If both ends of $u$ are the same generator, its own domain is periodic.

This assertion is proved from actual finite ordered lifts and local degree identities, without an index formula, a Chern pairing or a surjectivity assertion about arbitrary region domains. It makes no claim that every periodic domain or continuous Whitney class has a holomorphic representative.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(\Sigma,j)$ be a closed Riemann surface with positive area form $\eta$, and put $X=\operatorname{Sym}^m(\Sigma)$, $m\ge1$, with its induced complex structure $J_0$. Let $q:\Sigma^m\to X$ be the quotient, $\Delta\subset X$ its repeated-point locus, and $\Omega=\sum_{l=1}^m\operatorname{pr}_l^*\eta$. Off $\Delta$ the permutation-invariant form $\Omega$ descends to a smooth form $\omega$ on $X\setminus\Delta$. Equip $X$ with any smooth Riemannian metric $g$.

Let $L_\alpha,L_\beta$ be product tori formed from two finite systems of pairwise disjoint attaching curves, with transverse intersections between the systems. Suppose a smooth path $J_t$ agrees with $J_0$ on a neighborhood $V$ of $\Delta$ and tames $\omega$ on $X\setminus V$. Let $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to X$ be a smooth $J_t$-holomorphic strip, with boundary on these tori, finite $g$-Dirichlet energy, and uniform limits at both ends to intersection generators. For each complementary region $R$ of the attaching curves write $n_R(u)$ for the signed intersection multiplicity of $u$ with $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{m-1}(\Sigma)$ at a generic $p\in R$.

There is a constant $C$ depending only on the fixed geometric data and the path, independent of $u$, such that
$$E_g(u)=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R\times[0,1]}(|u_s|_g^2+|u_t|_g^2)\,dsdt\le C\sum_R n_R(u)\int_R\eta.$$
In particular energies of all such representatives with one fixed domain are uniformly bounded. The finite-energy hypothesis here is explicit; no assertion that arbitrary asymptotically convergent smooth solutions automatically have finite energy is included.

derivations.claim: In genus zero the target is one point and every strip is constant with zero domain and zero energy, so all conclusions hold with $E_0=1$; in the family assertion this remains so for every path. Assume henceforth positive genus. For two strips with the same ordered ends, [F2] makes $P=D(u)-D(v)$ periodic. Its basepoint coefficient is zero because both strips have $n_z=0$. By [F1] it vanishes. Thus their actual domains agree, whether their interior almost complex paths coincide or merely satisfy the common data of the Statement. If the ends of a strip agree, [F2] makes its own domain periodic with basepoint coefficient zero, so [F1] makes it zero. The energy inequality [F3] then forces its nonnegative energy to be zero. A smooth map with zero Dirichlet energy on the connected strip has zero derivatives everywhere and is constant. [F1, F2, F3, given, construct, algebra]

There are finitely many generators, since opposite-system curves have finitely many transverse intersections and a generator is one of finitely many possible matching tuples. Hence there are finitely many ordered endpoint pairs. For each pair admitting a strip in the specified set choose one actual strip and its domain; this uses only a finite number of choices. Step 1.1 says that the domain $D_{xy}$ thereby chosen is common to every actual strip with those ends. Each of the finitely many numbers $$C\sum_R n_R(D_{xy})\int_R\eta$$ is finite, since the region set is finite and its coefficients are integers. It is nonnegative whenever such a strip exists, by [F3]. Their finite maximum, enlarged by one, is a uniform upper bound $E_0$. If there are no such endpoint pairs, set $E_0=1$. For a family of paths the same argument uses its one common $C$ and the same finite endpoint-pair domains from step 1.1. No choice of one strip per homotopy class or per parameter was made. [F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

We verify the stated local uniformity of $C$. Choose a smaller diagonal neighborhood $V_0$ with closure in the fixed integrable neighborhood $V$. On the compact complement $X\setminus V_0$, the descended product two-form is smooth. The fixed allowed background path has a positive uniform minimum of $\omega(v,J_tv)$ over unit vectors there: outside $V$ this is its tameness, and on $V\setminus V_0$ it is the positive product form with the fixed standard complex structure. Compactness of the parameter interval and unit sphere bundle gives the minimum. A sufficiently small $C^0$ change in $J_t$, supported off the fixed integrable neighborhoods, preserves at least half this minimum and gives a common upper bound for $|J_t|$. The pointwise estimate $$\tfrac12(|v|_g^2+|J_tv|_g^2)\le c\,\omega(v,J_tv)$$ consequently has one common $c$ on that complement. On the integrable part $V_0$, the product metric, the quotient map derivative bound and the standard complex structure are fixed. These are exactly the two constants used in [F3]'s actual ordered-cover energy proof. Taking their fixed maximum therefore supplies one common $C$ for all paths in this neighborhood. Step 2.1 applies, completing the uniform energy and constant-self-strip conclusions without a Fredholm-domain formula, genericity or Floer invariance assertion. [F3, step 2.1, construct, algebra] ∎
